what: Naming the node that substituted its input, predicted before it was built
written: 2026-08-22, before zk/input_check.py had a per-party variant
the_observation: The dealer ALREADY publishes what is needed. qomm_transport/roles.py Dealing carries share_commitments --- one commitment per share per value --- so that check_share works and so that adds_up can catch a dealer whose shares do not sum. Those are exactly the commitments a per-party check combines. The marginal cost of naming is therefore the openings, not the commitments.
the_construction: Today the circuit opens one combination over the reconstructed values: s = sum_j c_j v_j + m, and the verifier checks it against the homomorphic combination of the value commitments. Detection, no name. Instead open one combination PER PARTY over that party's own inputs: s_p = sum_j c_j x_{p,j} + m_p, checked against sum_j c_j C_{p,j} + C_{m_p}. A party whose check fails is named, by anyone, from published data. And sum_p s_p is the old check, so the new one is strictly stronger.

predictions.predicted: about 160 bits, NARROWER than the current 164
predictions.arithmetic: party p's combination is over shares, which are value_bits + SLACK_BITS = 71 bits, so the combination is 71 + 40 + 8 = 119 and its mask 159. But the mask is party p's own input and is NOT split across nodes, so it does not pay the 40 bits of share slack plus log2(7) that made the current mask need 164.

predictions.predicted: a substituting party is named with probability at least 1 - 2^-40, the same argument as the aggregate check: the coefficients come from the commitments, so an error has to be chosen before its cancelling coefficient can be seen

predictions.quantity: can a dealer frame an honest node?
predictions.predicted: no, and it is detectable before the run rather than after. If the dealer commits to a share it did not send, the node's check_share fails and it can refuse to compute, holding the signature as evidence; and adds_up catches shares that do not sum to the committed value.

what_this_still_does_not_do: It names the party that fed a different value. It does not stop it, and it does not make the quote correct --- the run has already computed on the wrong input by the time the opening is checked. This is rung 4, public accountability, not rung 5.
